svg.title: Where Git Carries It — and Where It Doesn't
svg.desc: Local optimistic rewind is enough when the world is small and reversible; it breaks for concurrency, uncommitted work, merge interplay, effects outside git, .git surgery, and untracked state.
svg.text: Where Git Carries It — and Where It Doesn't
Local optimistic rewind works because the world is usually small and reversible. Until it isn't.
FORGIVING — the common case
you committed
git reflog recovers from any reset --hard; the harness's snapshot is just a faster path
one agent, one checkout
its private store + git is more than enough
each agent gets its own git worktree
different working trees, no index races, merge at the end like two branches
— this is the multi-agent answer
the thing changed is just code
almost any local mistake is recoverable
NOT FORGIVING — the local journal is useless here
uncommitted changes + a destructive git command
reset --hard / stash drop → gone, and not in the reflog (which tracks committed
refs, not working-tree state) — only the snapshot, if it has it
merge conflicts — the interplay itself
the conflict lives in the *relationship between two histories* — rewinding one
agent can't un-conflict it with another; resolve by hand, or with a 3rd run
concurrent ops on one .git
.git/index.lock races; A's restore clobbers B — needs worktrees or a lease
on the checkout (coordination through journaled state — no harness does it)
effects outside git
push (it's on the remote), npm publish, PR comments, CI runs, deploys, a charge
from running the test suite — rewind touches only the local tree
.git surgery
gc --prune, filter-repo, force-push prune the reflog itself — even "git is your net" collapses
untracked / ignored state
node_modules · .env · dist/ · a local DB — git-based snapshots skip them; restore = code at T, deps at T+5
The boundary: one actor + local edits = forgiving.

A second actor / a remote / CI / a publish / a deploy = the durable-execution machinery, for real. "The merchant's idempotency layer was already there" → "git's object store and reflog were already there." It's a floor, not a ceiling.
